answer: In an agent marketplace, agents such as lotus, cedar and ember must each lock a $100 bond for every active bidding identity, with withdrawals delayed for 30 days. Creating accounts is free, but only bonded accounts can bid, so an attacker running 1,000 fake bidders must immobilize $100,000. The withdrawal delay prevents recycling one bond across many identities during an auction, making a swarm costly in capital.
